liability.quote: It is not necessary to prove intention to commit academic misconduct and all cases will be considered in line with this policy, regardless of whether the misconduct was intentional.
However, proven intent to commit academic misconduct is likely to be considered an aggravating factor when considering potential outcomes.
Poor academic practice involves an unintentional misunderstanding of scholarly practice.

detection.quote: Staff may use the electronic software “TurnitinUK” or other means to assist them in the process of detecting academic misconduct.

it is appropriate to ask the student to explain their answers, ideas, concepts or references.

process.quote: The meeting is not a hearing, and the meeting should be informal, supportive and exploratory.
A suspected case of academic misconduct may be referred to a Misconduct Committee for the following reasons:
All concerns will be investigated in accordance with this policy and using the associated procedure.
If a student declines to engage with the AIM, they will have the opportunity to provide a written response.
Student Conduct & Appeals will review the information provided and determine whether the case requires a full hearing by a Misconduct Committee.
Proceedings under Stages 1-3 (below) are not invalidated or postponed due to the absence of the student, provided that the student has been given timely written notice of the AIM/Committee
The College understands that sometimes students make mistakes, and is committed to supporting all students, even where academic misconduct may have occurred.
Students may appeal the decision of a Misconduct Committee on either of both of the following grounds:

Students should submit a Misconduct Appeal Form to the Associate Director, Student Conduct & Appeals (or their nominee), on behalf of the Vice Chancellor & President, within 10 working days of the date of the Misconduct Committee outcome.
All cases will be considered on the balance of probabilities.
The outcome should be recorded by the Faculty/Department, including a summary of what was discussed in the AIM, all relevant evidence considered, and reasons for the outcome determined.

outcomes.quote: Under a Stage One AIM, Educative Outcomes or Restorative Outcomes (a)-(d) may be applied.
a formal warning, with those parts of the student's work that are unaffected by the concern to be marked
a formal warning, with those parts of the student's work that are unaffected by the concern to be marked, and the assessment result capped at the pass mark.
the cancellation of the results in an assessment/s and a mark of zero returned
the requirement that the student resubmit an amended version of the assessment.
A student’s final award will be withheld whilst any action is being taken under this policy.
All second instances where academic misconduct was upheld in the first instance, should be referred to Stage Two: Misconduct Committee (below).
proven intent to commit academic misconduct is likely to be considered an aggravating factor when considering potential outcomes.
a recommendation to the Academic Board that the student’s award be revoked
the College may report the student to that body under Academic Regulation 8.29.

definitions.quote: Academic Misconduct is the adoption of working methods that are outside the spirit of the College regulations and the values of academic integrity.
Third party involvement: when a student receives unauthorized assistance from a third party which results in the submission of an individual assessment
Third party production: when work submitted is substantively the product of a third party.
Poor academic practice involves an unintentional misunderstanding of scholarly practice.
Provision of contract cheating services: providing, or arranging for another person to provide, contract cheating services for financial gain to students.
